success_patterns: Verbatim or near-verbatim clue matches decided the answer. The clue sentence appeared in many passages with one slot blanked ('Only the arrival of the Cunard liner Carpathia...'). Archive lines such as 'clue | answer' appeared in the context ('Hopefully you didn't get this music... | Raindrops Keep Fallin' On My Head'). Truncated archive snippets were completed from other passages that tied the same facts together (the antiseptics clue -> Joseph Lister). All of this is already covered by Rule 3.

The agent identified the slot type correctly and gave the bare entity: the person for a date-and-place fragment (Ronald Reagan), the real name for a nickname clue (Walter Cronkite), the title character with its regnal numeral (Richard III), the headword for a definition clue (insulator), and the generic dish for a description clue (burrito). This is already covered by Rules 1, 2 and 4.

Answers were short and dropped leading articles ('Carpathia', 'insulator', 'burrito') even though the gold forms had 'the/an/a'. Matching still succeeded, so the existing 'no added articles' and 'bare core answer' guidance works and needs no change.

When passages were noisy or off-topic (the Chipotle clue), the agent answered from its own knowledge with the plain common noun and did not copy a branded item from the passages. This is already covered by Strategic guidance sections 2 and 5.

patch.reasoning: Every success pattern in this batch is already encoded in Rules 1-4 and the strategic block.
